rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and map the elution window across most of the solvent range. This gives a first read on whether peaks are unretained, trapped to the high-organic hold, or clustered in a narrower phi region for later optimization.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only improvement is reducing t_last below 10 min while keeping every compound inside the gradient. The observed peaks span roughly phi_e about 0.11 to 0.59, so a trimmed, steeper window centered on that range should preserve resolution and pull the last peak earlier.

Resolution still has comfortable margin, so push for a shorter last peak by increasing temperature and using a slightly steeper, slightly higher-end gradient to accelerate the late compound. Keeping phi0 at 0.15 avoids making the first peaks too unretained while phi1 0.70 helps ensure the last peak stays in-gradient or reaches the hold sooner.

The limiting pair 6/7 lost resolution mainly from the temperature increase, while run time is now comfortably under 10 min. Step temperature back toward 40 C and keep a short trimmed gradient to recover selectivity for that pair while aiming to stay under the 10 min threshold.

The 6/7 pair is clearly temperature-sensitive, with best selectivity at 40 C so far; returning to 40 C should restore full resolution. Using the shorter 10 min gradient instead of 12 min tests whether we can keep all pairs at or above 1.5 while bringing the last peak closer to 10 min for a higher CRF than injection 2.

Probe whether the gradient can be shortened further while retaining full resolution, since the current optimum has some margin on the critical 6/7 pair (R 1.58) and t_last remains below 10 min. If resolution holds, this would identify a faster equally optimal method; if not, it brackets the lower limit of usable steepness.

Since steepening to 8 min hurt only the critical 6/7 pair, try narrowing the gradient window instead at the proven 10 min and 40 C to keep separation strength while trimming the high-organic range the mixture does not use. The peaks from injection 5 span roughly phi_e about 0.17 to 0.60, so phi1 0.60 should still keep the last peak in-gradient and may preserve full resolution with a slightly more focused program.

The best method is already optimal on CRF, so this run should map robustness rather than chase a higher score. Raising both phi0 and phi1 by 0.05 keeps the gradient width the same but shifts the active window to slightly stronger elution, testing whether the early peaks remain acceptably retained while the last peak moves even earlier without sacrificing the critical 6/7 separation.

The critical 6/7 pair worsened when the whole window was shifted to higher organic, suggesting selectivity improves at lower phi. Lower phi0 while keeping tG and temperature at the proven optimum should slightly flatten the gradient over the active region and may increase margin on 6/7 while likely keeping t_last under 10 min.

Injection 9 reached the score ceiling but left the critical pair only barely above threshold, so increase phi1 slightly to bring the late peak earlier while keeping the lower phi0 that helped 6/7. This tests whether a bit more high-organic strength can preserve full resolution and still stay under 10 min with more margin on runtime.

Lowering phi0 improved the critical 6/7 pair from injection 8 to 9, so test one more step down while keeping the successful phi1 and tG. This should strengthen selectivity around the crowded middle region, and the late peak should still remain under 10 min because phi1 stays at 0.65.

The critical 6/7 pair is strongly temperature-sensitive and has only modest margin at the best 40 C method, so explore a cooler run where selectivity may improve. Extending tG to 12 min compensates for the lower temperature’s longer retention while checking whether extra resolution headroom appears for that pair.

We already have CRF 1.000, so use remaining runs to map a nearby robustness corner with a narrower, higher-organic window at the proven 40 C. This tests whether the method can stay fully resolved while moving the last peak earlier, and whether the critical pair remains acceptable when both the window is shifted up and slightly narrowed.

Probe the orthogonal tradeoff between extra gradient time and higher temperature around the successful window: longer tG may restore the critical 6/7 separation while 45 C may still keep the run under 10 min. This tests whether a different balance of slope and temperature can also reach the CRF ceiling with more speed margin.

The two ceiling methods suggest lower phi0 helps the critical 6/7 pair, while lower phi1 improves its margin but can push the last peak later. This combination tests whether keeping the favorable low phi0 with a slightly lower phi1 can still keep t_last under 10 min while maintaining full resolution.

Use the stronger 6/7 selectivity seen at low phi0, but pair it with a longer gradient and 45 C to see whether higher temperature can pull the last peak earlier without losing full resolution. This explores whether the temperature penalty on 6/7 can be offset by the more favorable phi window and shallower slope.

The main unresolved question near the optimum is whether a slightly higher phi1 can offset the extra retention of the 12 min gradient without collapsing the critical 6/7 pair at 40 C. This run explores a shallower slope with stronger final elution, which could keep full resolution and perhaps still land just under 10 min.

Among 40 C runs, lowering phi0 tends to help the critical 6/7 pair while lowering phi1 also improves that pair but risks a time penalty; this point combines both effects to map that corner directly. It should show whether extra selectivity can be gained there and how much t_last moves relative to the two current ceiling methods.

The optimum score is already achieved, so use a remaining run to define the lower-temperature robustness limit at the best gradient shape. This isolates temperature as the variable at the winning method and will show whether the 6/7 selectivity improves or if a different pair becomes limiting when retention increases.

Both ceiling methods at 10 min show only modest margin on the critical 6/7 pair, so test whether the lower-phi0 optimum can tolerate the steeper 8 min gradient any better than the 0.15 start. This directly probes whether low phi0 helps enough to preserve full resolution in a faster method.

Most remaining uncertainty is about whether stronger final organic can compensate for the loss of separation from a short gradient. This run checks the fast/high-phi1 corner at 40 C, clarifying whether the last peak can be accelerated without worsening the already critical 6/7 pair beyond the 8 min, 0.65-end method.

We have not directly tested whether the narrower 0.45-wide window at the higher start can balance the opposing effects seen for 0.20/0.60 and 0.20/0.70. This midpoint should clarify how much of the 6/7 behavior comes from phi1 versus total window width while staying close to the proven 10 min, 40 C regime.

With only a few runs left and the score ceiling already reached, use one to extend the phi1 trend from the low-phi0 optimum and see how aggressively the last peak can be accelerated before the critical 6/7 pair collapses. This helps define the high-organic robustness boundary around the best-performing region.

A final unexplored corner is a higher start with a narrower window, which may keep the run comfortably short while sharpening selectivity in the active region differently from the broader 0.20-start methods. This brackets robustness on the high-phi0 side around the successful 10 min, 40 C regime.

The last run showed phi0 0.25 makes the first pair dangerously unretained, so for the final injection test whether increasing phi1 alone can shorten the late peak while leaving the early-pair problem essentially unchanged. This cleanly isolates phi1’s effect at the highest phi0 explored and completes the robustness map on that boundary.
